item.title: Kusatsu Yumomi Performance: The Rhythmic Art of Cooling Hot Spring Water — Guide
item.description: Yumomi (‘hot water kneading’) is a traditional method developed in Kusatsu to cool the town’s naturally scalding, over 50°C spring water to a bathable temperature without diluting its mineral concentration, performed by stirring the water with large wooden paddles in a coordinated rhythm. At the historic Netsu-no-Yu bathhouse, performers in traditional dress demonstrate the technique on stage several times daily, accompanied by a folk song, turning a practical necessity into an entertaining cultural show that visitors can also try their hand at.
